notes: Corrected the second genitive phrase, γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων → 'and of the chief women'. The accepted alignment gave 'of the' to the postposed τῶν under rule 21, but rule 57 sends an article that follows its noun to rule 31, and rule 31 leaves the determiner on the noun, supplying one there when the noun is anarthrous. So γυναικῶν takes the discontinuous 'of the … women' headed on the noun, τῶν is unrepresented, and πρώτων keeps a bare 'chief'.

The first genitive phrase is unaffected, its article standing in front of Ἑλλήνων, so 'of the' remains there; the Greek differs in article placement, which is what licenses the two analyses side by side (rules 24, 56).
Both τε particles stay aligned because the ASV writes two English 'and's and no καί answers either of them (rule 70).
